forces.title: Weak mortgage lending indicates slowing housing market momentum.
forces.description: Belgium's housing market, despite recent resilience, faces slowing momentum due to weak mortgage lending. The number of new mortgages in the first eight months of 2026 was approximately 10% below the level recorded in the previous year. This significant decline in financing activity acts as a high-impact headwind, suggesting that overall housing demand will temper in the upcoming quarters, ultimately leading to a cooler market and reduced growth opportunities for housing finance providers.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Elevated interest rates constrain housing market financing conditions.
forces.description: Long-term interest rates have continued to rise since the start of geopolitical conflicts and are expected to remain restrictive. This sustained high-interest-rate environment directly impacts the affordability of mortgage financing, limiting borrowing capacity for potential homebuyers and increasing the cost of existing variable-rate mortgages. This financial constraint will contribute to a gradual cooling of the Belgian housing market, making financing conditions less favorable and reducing mortgage demand.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Rising energy costs boost value of energy-efficient homes.
forces.description: Higher energy prices, reinforced by increasingly stringent renovation standards, are causing a structural shift in the Belgian housing market. The financial benefits of energy-efficient housing are becoming more visible, widening the price gap with energy-intensive homes. This trend improves the economics of investments in insulation and efficient heating systems, simultaneously acting as a tailwind for demand in the energy-efficient segment and driving long-term marketability based on energy performance.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Irish housing investment hampered by taxation and rent-cap policies.
forces.description: Construction activity in Ireland continues to strengthen, yet the housing segment remains the weakest performer. This underperformance is directly attributed to existing taxation and rent-cap policies, which have significantly constrained investment in residential development across certain areas. Despite strong underlying demand, these regulatory and fiscal measures create a substantial headwind for increasing housing supply, indirectly impacting the pipeline for new mortgage origination and overall growth in housing finance.

forces.title: Robust underlying demand supports long-term Irish housing activity.
forces.description: Despite policy-induced investment constraints in residential construction, Ireland's housing segment benefits from strong underlying demand, which is expected to support activity over the longer term. This persistent and robust demand acts as a significant tailwind, indicating sustained interest and need for housing acquisition. This fundamental demand underpins future opportunities for housing finance providers, even in the face of current supply challenges, suggesting potential for growth once supply constraints ease.

forces.title: Elevated Irish house prices pose significant affordability challenge.
forces.description: Ireland's economic overview identifies "high house prices" as a notable risk within the structural business environment. This condition creates a significant affordability challenge for prospective homebuyers, directly impacting their ability to enter the housing market and secure mortgage finance. Elevated prices can restrict the pool of eligible borrowers by requiring larger down payments and higher income thresholds for loan qualification, posing a key risk to the volume and accessibility of housing finance.
forces.source_title: 2026 Ireland country risks: Strong tailwinds set to persist amid strong buffers

forces.title: Irish government targets 300K new homes to improve affordability.
forces.description: The Irish government has set an ambitious target to build 300,000 homes, coupled with energy upgrades, aimed at improving housing affordability. While progress has been slow, this policy commitment represents a strong long-term upside driver for the housing finance sector. Successful delivery of this target would significantly expand the available housing stock, stimulating demand for new mortgages and potentially easing price pressures, thus creating a more accessible and active market for housing finance providers.
forces.source_title: 2026 Ireland country risks: Strong tailwinds set to persist amid strong buffers

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing outlook challenging despite Q2 resilience, weakening demand.
viewpoints.description: ING Think observes unexpected resilience in the Belgian housing market during Q2 2026, with modest price increases (+0.2% QoQ, +5.3% YoY) and recovering transactions. However, this positive performance is deemed unsustainable. The underlying picture points to a challenging outlook due to significantly weaker mortgage production and persistently high interest rates. These factors are expected to cause housing demand to lose momentum in the coming quarters, leading to a gradual cooling of the market. Nominal median house prices are forecast to rise by only 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing
